purpose: make the system reachable by the right names, securely, with changes that are controlled and reversible
entry_criteria: Domain ownership and registrar access are known
Target endpoints and their addresses are defined
DNS provider and its access controls exist
procedure: Keep an inventory of domains, records and owners; remove records with no owner.
Define DNS records as code and review changes like any other change.
Restrict who can change DNS and require multi-factor authentication on the registrar and DNS accounts.
Set TTLs deliberately: lower them ahead of a planned change, restore afterward.
Enable protections: registrar lock, DNSSEC where supported, and checks for dangling records that point to released resources.
Verify with queries from outside after each change and monitor expiry of domains and certificates.
acceptance_criteria: Registrar lock and multi-factor authentication are enabled
No dangling records point at released resources
Expiry alerts exist for domains and certificates
validation_method: Cloud owner review of DNS changes.

validation.command: dig +short A app.example.com && dig +short CNAME www.example.com   # example

validation.check: list CNAME records whose targets no longer resolve

failure_modes.mode: Dangling record can be taken over
failure_modes.detection: CNAME points to a deleted service

worked_example: ILLUSTRATIVE: Before moving the app to a new load balancer, the team lowers the TTL to 60 seconds, changes the record through reviewed code, checks resolution from three networks, and raises the TTL again the next day.
